text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Security alert in three major cities.
- Prime Minister Netanyahu reportedly asked Syria, Iran to block terror attack.
- Troops kill two gunmen in south Lebanon.
- Panel on closing streets on Jewish sabbath to present recommendations today.
- Government to sell 10 percent of Bank Leumi on Wall Street, London exchange.
- Japanese business leaders back out of planned visit.
- Landys & Gyr to invest in Israel.
HAARETZ
- Israel demands Syria and Iran act to prevent militant attack on Israel.
- Damage caused economy by security alert on Sunday: 50 million shekels.
- Head of sabbath road inquiry committee: The more ultra- religious Jerusalem becomes, collapse possible.
- Deputy head of Russian security council apparently has Israeli citizenship.
- Israeli President upset at leaks from prime minister's office on his possible successors.
- Now okay for second and third level relations to donate organs.
- Dispute over moving military industries plants from coastal, central region to Negev desert.
MAARIV
- Warning to Syria, Iran and Libya: Don't aid militants who would attack Israel.
- Suspicion that deal to acquire five Panther helicopters for army from U.S. involved corruption to tune of $10 million.
- Netanyahu has decided that 540 dunams (55 hectares, 135 acres) in Jordan valley will be returned to cousin of King Hussein.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu to Germany: put pressure on Iran to prevent terror attack in Israel; Israel proposes mutual thinning of forces on Golan to lessen tension.
- Navy officer suspected of taking bribes to tune of $5 million over purchase of "Bat" helicopters.
- Director General of Bezeq could quit over Motorola affair.
GLOBES
- Damage of tens of millions of shekels to economy as result of security alert. SIE
